findings.title: Hung flusher process is never killed because the isinstance check never matches SpawnProcess
findings.body: `process.kill()` is now guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes come from `mp_context.Process` on a spawn context, which are `SpawnProcess` objects. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.context.Process`, so the isinstance check is False. When a flusher is declared hung (`cause == "hang"`), it is not killed and a replacement is started for the same shards. Two flushers then run on the same shards and the old one leaks. Repeated restarts accumulate orphaned processes, and duplicate segments can be flushed. The same wrong check in `join()` (line 346) means `terminate()` is never called either. Check against `threading.Thread` instead, or use `hasattr(process, 'kill')`.

findings.title: The added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: `test_basic` patches `time.sleep` to a no-op at the top, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added to "give flusher threads time to process" does not wait. The test still depends on thread scheduling to get the flushed message before `join()`, so it can be flaky. Use a real wait (poll until `messages` is non-empty, with a timeout), or capture the real sleep before patching.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name and comma-joined shard values
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` are tagged `shard`, but `wait_produce` is tagged `shards`. This makes the metrics hard to correlate and aggregate. The tag value is a comma-joined list of shards, which creates a new tag value for every distinct shard grouping. `flusher_unhealthy` uses a per-shard tag instead, so the conventions also differ across metrics.

findings.title: Unused method _create_process_for_shard
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` is not called anywhere. It would also restart a process without the kill or restart-count handling that `_ensure_processes_alive` does. Remove it.
